messages:
sarah_cust: Hey support — after the partial eu-west outage our production traffic started returning short, truncated completions and broken function calls. We see that some requests were routed to us-east and served a much smaller 'lite' model variant (rl3-lite-v1). Responses are missing tokens and the tokenizer seems to disagree with our client: function-calls are failing with 'bad tokenization' and we get hallucinated JSON. Example request-id: req_0a9f3c. Can we get help?

maria_support: Sorry you're seeing this. Can you paste a couple of raw request/response pairs (anonymized) and the request-id header? Also which model did you pin in the request?

sarah_cust: Sending two samples below. We call the hosted endpoint with model: "redwood-llm-3" and model_version: "2026-02-21". Headers show region: eu-west-1.

--- sample 1 ---
Request: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1' -H 'X-Request-ID: req_0a9f3c' "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-3","input":"Summarize: The user reported..."}'
Response (served variant): {"model":"rl3-lite-v1","text":"Summ. user reported... \uFFFD"}  <-- truncated tokens and invalid bytes

--- sample 2 (function call failure) ---
Request-id: req_0a9f3d
Request payload has a function spec, returned: {"name":"get_user","args":"\u0000..."} and JSON parse fails on client.

maria_support: Thanks. This looks like a tokenizer/config drift between redwood-llm-3 and rl3-lite-v1. I'm escalating to runtime and infra. Deepa, Ryan — assigning.

deepa_runtime: On it. Initial logs show that the smart-router attempted eu-west placements but capacity hit and triggered region-fallback to us-east. The router then applied variant-selection heuristics. It looks like a compatibility check flagged the lite variant as "compatible" incorrectly because the model family matches (rl3) despite different tokenizer configs.

ryan_infra: We found the routing decision in the trace for req_0a9f3c: 

[router] trace_id=req_0a9f3c route=(eu-west->us-east) reason=(capacity_spike) selected_variant=rl3-lite-v1 compat_check=true
[serve] selected_engine=quantized-int8 seq_len=2048 tokenizer=rl3-tokenizer-v2
[serve] WARNING: variant_tokenizer=rl3-lite-tokenizer-v1 != client_tokenizer=rl3-tokenizer-v2

maria_support: Is this a regression in compatibility checks or a data/config mismatch in variant metadata?

deepa_runtime: Looks like regression: a recent metadata sync (2026-03-12) started tagging 'compatible=true' for lite variants when family==rl3 and major_version==3, but we missed a tokenizer_version field in the check. I'm preparing a hotfix to include tokenizer_version equality in compat logic.

sarah_cust: Appreciate that. What's the recommended mitigation now? We're getting customer-facing failures.

deepa_runtime: Immediate mitigations: 1) Add a routing override to disallow rl3-lite-* variants for your org (we can apply a per-customer ban). 2) Pin region to eu-west-only for now (reduces failover but might queue). 3) We'll push a hotfix to the router to enforce tokenizer_version equality — ETA ~45m. Which would you prefer?

sarah_cust: Please apply a per-customer ban on lite variants and pin region to eu-west for us. We'll accept higher latency rather than broken outputs.

maria_support: Done — I created support action S-8482: applied variant_blacklist=["rl3-lite-v1","rl3-lite-v2"] for org org_9982 and set routing_policy=region_strict:euw. Confirmed by deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: action=S-8482 apply_blacklist org=org_9982 variants=[rl3-lite-v1,rl3-lite-v2] result=success
deploy-bot: routing_policy=region_strict:euw result=success

ryan_infra: While we patch the compat checks, note this is P2 (customer-impacting). Incident created.

incident-bot: incident=INC-2026-03-17-47 severity=P2 owners=[runtime,router,infra] status=investigating

maria_support: After blacklist was applied did you see errors drop, Sarah?

sarah_cust: Verified for the last 25 requests — function calls and completions look normal. Thank you. A few requests still delayed but not broken.

deepa_runtime: Hotfix for compat logic is staged and rolling: change is to compare tokenizer_version metadata and only allow fallback when tokenizer_version matches OR when variant has a tokenizer_compat shim. Also adding audit logs for variant selection. Rolling now.

ryan_infra: Patch completed, router now rejects rl3-lite variants for any request with tokenizer mismatch. We also added an alert to catch future cases: alert if selected_variant.tokenizer != requested.tokenizer and compat_check==true.

maria_support: Logged postmortem action items: 1) add tokenizer_version to variant metadata validation, 2) backfill missing metadata for all variants, 3) per-org default policy to prefer capability parity on failover. Assigned to runtime + model-onboarding.

sarah_cust: Thanks everyone. Could you send a short incident summary and any recommended config changes we should make on our side?

maria_support: Will send summary (S-8482) and recommended configs: pin model_version, set routing preference to region_strict if you require exact parity on failover, and enable "reject_on_incompatible_fallback" if you want 4xx instead of silent variant swaps.

sarah_cust: Perfect. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :heart:

maria_support: Closing thread, will attach postmortem once runtime publishes it. If you need further help ping me or reopen S-8482.
